% A REAL Beamer deck written for pdfpc -- the fixture for ADR-0048 §4 and §5: \pdfpcnote's hidden /Text
% annotations (one copy per overlay page; their string encoding depends on the engine, below) and the pdfpc keys
% pdfpc.sty writes into the XMP packet (a NESTED rdf:Description inside hyperxmp's, which is not valid RDF/XML).
% beamer-pdfpc.pdfpc beside it is its sidecar, written by hand in pdfpc 4.7.0's writer format (pdfpc itself was not
% installed). It disagrees with the XMP on purpose, so precedence can be tested: duration 30, lastMinutes 2 and
% endSlide 1 all lose to the XMP. It holds a note on page 0 that differs from that page's annotation (both are shown,
% ADR-0048 §4), a note on page 3, and page 4 hidden. pdfpc's writer never saves a page whose note came from an
% annotation, so a note beside an annotation is what a sidecar holds after the author added the \pdfpcnote later.
%
% Two PDFs were compiled from this file on 2026-10-17, each in its own empty directory and each TWICE (see
% "Measured" below for why), with beamer.cls 2026/01/22 v3.77, pdfpc.sty 2023/10/21 v0.7.1 and hyperxmp.sty v5.13:
%   beamer-pdfpc.pdf         This is LuaHBTeX, Version 1.24.0 (TeX Live 2026/Arch Linux)
%                              lualatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error beamer-pdfpc.tex   (twice)
%   beamer-pdfpc-pdftex.pdf  pdfTeX 3.141592653-2.6-1.40.29 (TeX Live 2026/Arch Linux)
%                              pdflatex -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error beamer-pdfpc.tex   (twice; renamed)
% and they are committed as-is: frozen samples of real TeX output. Do not regenerate them to "fix" a test.
%
% Expected, written down before the first compile (pages are 0-based):
%   pages 5: One o1, One o2, Two, Three, Four; labels 1 1 2 3 4
%   annotations: /Text with /F 6 on pages 0 and 1 (the same note), and on page 2
%   XMP: pdfpc:Duration 20, pdfpc:EndTime 10:30, pdfpc:EndUserSlide 3, pdfpc:LastMinutes 3,
%        pdfpc:NotesPosition none (guessed: no pgfpages layout), pdfpc:DisableMarkdown false
%
% Measured (2026-10-17), where it differed from the expectation above:
%   * ONE pass gave 6 pages, the last LaTeX's "Temporary page!": hyperxmp learns the page count from the .aux, so a
%     pdfpc deck needs a second pass. The second pass has the 5 pages and the labels expected, under both engines.
%     A separate one-pass LuaLaTeX compile (its expectation registered first) showed that the XMP already carries the
%     six keys, and that the extra page is labelled 4 (labels 1 1 2 3 4 4): it joins the last frame as an overlay.
%   * `\\` is a newline only under pdfTeX. Under LuaTeX, pdfpc.sty turns the note into hex BEFORE it redefines `\\`,
%     so the annotation carries the two characters `\\`, which is also the text pdfpc receives.
%   * Under pdfTeX, pdfpc.sty writes the note's UTF-8 bytes into a literal string, which every reader decodes as
%     PDFDocEncoding: `café` arrives as `cafÃ©` (the bytes are C3 A9). Under LuaTeX it is UTF-16BE hex, and correct.
%   Everything else was as expected: /Text with /F 6 on pages 0, 1 and 2, and the six XMP keys.
%   * XeLaTeX (XeTeX 3.141592653-2.6-0.999998, twice; that PDF is not committed): `\\` is a newline, and
%     xdvipdfmx re-encodes the non-ASCII note as UTF-16BE hex itself, so café and naïve arrive correct: only a
%     pdfTeX deck needs the repair (ADR-0048 §4). Registered before the compile; all three expectations held.
\documentclass{beamer}
\usepackage[duration=20,endtime=10:30,enduserslide=3,lastminutes=3]{pdfpc}
\title{pdfpc fixture}
\begin{document}
\begin{frame}{One}
  One first point \pause One second point
  \pdfpcnote{A pdfpc note on both overlays of frame one\\with a second line, café and naïve}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Two}
  Two words
  \pdfpcnote{Markdown with *emphasis* and a [link](https://example.org/)}
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Three}
  Three words
\end{frame}
\begin{frame}{Four}
  Four words
\end{frame}
\end{document}
